messages:
alex: quick heads up — onboarding Vesper9B (9B decoder). ran int4 quant pipeline and our embedding sims vs fp16 dropped ~0.035 on the standard 10k-sim test. Suspect vocab normalization interaction + rotary headwise scaling.

maria: numbers? short reproduction? :eyes:

alex: pasted the minimal repro below. baseline fp16 avg cosine = 0.912, int4 avg cosine = 0.877.

jon: that's pretty big for int4. do you see the same for raw logits / perplexity?

alex: perplexity is within noise for short prompts (±1.2%), but embedding-space measures and a few downstream recall tasks show regressions.

kai: can you share tokenizer normalization mode? NFC vs NFKC often bites us with onnx conversions.

alex: we used our standard normalizer (NFKC) pipeline. interestingly, converting to NFC before tokenization moves the avg cos to 0.889 for int4. so there is some coupling.

alex: repro snippet:
```
# eval snippet
python -m redwood.eval.embed_compare \
  --model vesper9b --precision int4 --normalizer nfkc \
  --input corpus/10k-sim.jsonl --batch 64 --seed 42
```
output (truncated):
```
baseline (fp16) avg_cos: 0.9123
int4 (nfkc) avg_cos: 0.8771
int4 (nfc)  avg_cos: 0.8892
```

eva: that delta narrowing with NFC is a tell. Could be tokenizer byte->unicode mapping causing subtle token id shifts which then change rotary phase alignment?

jon: also check kv-cache token id offsets on generation with long context. If token ids shift by sentinel positions we get headwise misalignment in rotary angles when we pack heads differently during quant run.

kai: I remember a case where our int4 quant lib reordered head dims for better alignment, and that showed up as headwise scale drift. Have you dumped a small layer's qk rotary matrices?

alex: yep — dumped first cross-attn rotary cos/sin matrices pre- and post-quant. phase vectors match up to float tolerances, but when we reorder head dims in layout (NHWC <-> NCHW-ish) the per-head scale stats diverge. small example diff:
```
head 0 mean(abs(diff)) = 3.1e-5  # ok
head 7 mean(abs(diff)) = 1.2e-2  # suspicious
```

maria: are we applying headwise scaling after quant or before? ordering matters.

alex: pre-quant we apply a per-head scale clamp then run quant. int4 path currently fuses clamp+pack in a single kernel which assumed canonical head order. If tokenizer normalization changes tokenization lengths, packing edge-case branches flip and kernel picks alternate layout.

jon: so it's a control-flow/packing prob, not fundamental rotary math. still, tokenizer mode toggles path. nasty.

alex: next steps I ran locally:
- force canonical head order in quant pack -> int4 cos sim up to 0.903
- force NFC normalizer at tokenization -> 0.892
- both fixes -> 0.907 (close to baseline but not identical)

kai: good triage. please open a minimal repro and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml. include the dumped matrices and a short note on quant kernel assumptions.

eva: will also add a small eval to the CI embed-smoke that compares int4 vs fp16 at a 1k subset so we catch regressions automatically. propose threshold avg_cos >= 0.90 for gate.

alex: created lightweight issue: https://redwood/issue/INF-2418 — includes repro and dumps. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml.

ci-bot: build 2026.03.21/1257 for "vesper9b-int4-onboard" completed — unit tests passed. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — assigning to jon and kai for runtime kernel follow-up. I can own tokenizer normalization switch if we want to default to NFC for onboarding flows to avoid false negatives.

jon: I'll take the kernel-side fix. will try to remove layout-dependent branches or make pack aware of normalizer-mode.

kai: I'll run quant pack audit and add fuzz tests for head reordering permutations.

alex: awesome. one last note — embedding drift mostly hits long-tail unicode cases (zero-width joiners, some emoji sequences). attaching a small list in the issue.

eva: good capture. putting a quick PR to CI in case we need immediate gating. :rocket:
